### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/core`, `@objectstack/service-messaging`, touching **10** documentable anchor(s).

**1** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/automation/webhooks.mdx`  _(via MessagingServicePlugin (symbol, a top-level class))_

⛔ **3** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v14.mdx`  _(via MessagingServicePlugin (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-5.mdx`  _(via MessagingServicePlugin (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/releases/v18/18-2.mdx`  _(via resolveLocalizationContext (symbol, a top-level function))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **3** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **58** of **210** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **39** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 481ade61c9c8369a78a0350090f6b204900a06c6` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `b9125d677dc95a4990015e83c728cf4c84011601` — the merge of head `4397f06d5f45b7ffbdc6ed0ba68749b26fadfe0b` into base `481ade61c9c8369a78a0350090f6b204900a06c6`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin b9125d677dc95a4990015e83c728cf4c84011601 && git checkout b9125d677dc95a4990015e83c728cf4c84011601
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 481ade61c9c8369a78a0350090f6b204900a06c6 4397f06d5f45b7ffbdc6ed0ba68749b26fadfe0b && git checkout -B drift-repro 481ade61c9c8369a78a0350090f6b204900a06c6 && git merge --no-ff 4397f06d5f45b7ffbdc6ed0ba68749b26fadfe0b

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 481ade61c9c8369a78a0350090f6b204900a06c6
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 481ade61c9c8369a78a0350090f6b204900a06c6` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `aef05cf6dafd9b1b109ff4cf909049cbf3ba46b0`
Local-runs: none
Scope: .changeset/27257-localization-read-failed.md, packages/core/src/security/resolve-authz-context.ts, packages/core/src/security/resolve-authz-context.test.ts, packages/core/src/security/resolve-localization-cache.test.ts, packages/core/src/security/resolve-localization-read-failed.test.ts, packages/services/service-messaging/src/email-channel.ts, packages/services/service-messaging/src/inbox-channel.ts, packages/services/service-messaging/src/messaging-service-plugin.ts, packages/services/service-messaging/src/template-tenant-currency.test.ts + packages/core/src/security/assemble-execution-context.ts (`EntryLocalization`, `entryFields`), packages/core/src/security/request-execution-context.ts, packages/core/src/security/organization-reach.ts and `localizationFallbackReach` / `resolveGuestOrganization` in the resolver file (the reach the direct read is scoped by), packages/core/src/security/index.ts (the export path), packages/mcp/src/plugin.ts (`resolveStdioExecutionContext`, the localization memo), packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/audit-plugin.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-plugin.ts and mail-tenant-currency.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-hono-server/src/current-user-endpoints.ts (`resolveCurrentUserLocalization`), packages/services/service-automation/src/plugin.ts, run-resume.ts and engine.ts (`setTenantCurrencyResolver`), packages/services/service-messaging/src/dispatcher.ts, backoff.ts, channel.ts, index.ts, sms-channel.ts (the grading, the retry ladder, the package entry, the other channels), packages/formula/src/template-engine.ts (`currencyDefaultRefusal`, the sentence the channel's rewrite stands in for), content/docs/automation/email-templates.mdx and content/docs/kernel/runtime-services/email-service.mdx (read for the claims they make; prose, not reviewed). Written at 2026-10-29T21:37Z; the check-run and review readings below were taken at 2026-10-29T21:35Z.

### ① Derived judgments

Each accept-set and public-surface change the diff implies, read against the cited code on this head:

1. **`@objectstack/core` — `resolveLocalizationContext`'s result gains `readFailed?: true` — right, and minimal.** The alias `LocalizationResult` is not exported; the surface is the return type of the exported function (`security/index` → package root). One optional key, literal `true`, absent on every successful answer; no input change, no new export name. The seven callers, each read: `request-execution-context.ts` assigns the answer to `EntryLocalization` (structurally assignable; the key is carried at runtime) and the shared assembler `entryFields` copies `timezone` / `locale` / `currency` by name, so `ExecutionContext` never carries it; `mcp/plugin.ts` memoizes the promise and hands it to `resolveStdioExecutionContext`, which calls that same assembler; `plugin-audit` destructures `locale`; `plugin-auth` reads `.currency`; the hono `/auth/me/localization` handler copies the three fields into its response; `service-automation` reads `.currency`; `service-messaging` is this PR. None spreads, deep-equals, serialises or persists the object, so no HTTP response, i18n payload, run context or delivery row sees the key except where this PR writes a sentence about it. `Type Check · workspace / source gates / consumer gates` and `TypeScript Type Check` are green on this head.
2. **The failure memo keeps the kind, and only the kind it should — right.** The flagged object is built once (`backendFailed ? { ...read, readFailed: true } : read`) and stored as the failure entry's `value`; the hit path returns `hit.value`, so a hit inside the 30 s TTL carries the flag (pinned twice in core, twice in messaging). The success entry stores the unflagged `read`, so no success is ever cached with the flag. `LOCALIZATION_FAILURE_CACHE_TTL_MS`, `localizationEntryIsLive` (a failure entry stays live until its TTL) and `putLocalizationEntry` are untouched. `backendFailed` is set at the one `sys_setting` catch only; the five settings-service legs still set nothing (#11877, pinned with `getMany` throwing in front of a successful empty direct read). A stale failure returned after a later success is unreachable within one key — a live hit returns before any read, and another key is another entry; the up-to-30 s "still failed" window after the backend recovers existed before this PR and now lands on the ladder's 1 s / 10 s / 60 s retries, the third of which is past the TTL. A non-cacheable `ql` gets the flag on the fresh answer and nothing stored.
3. **`@objectstack/service-messaging` — `getTenantCurrency` rejects on `readFailed`, answers `undefined` on a successful read with no default — right.** The public `EmailChannelOptions.getTenantCurrency` / `InboxChannelOptions.getTenantCurrency` signatures are unchanged (their JSDoc now states the rejection). Both channels read the currency BEFORE the render `try`, so a rejection cannot be mistaken for a render refusal, then render with the `currency` key omitted — the same render a failed read produced before this PR. `templateRefusalAfterCurrencyReadFault` is a module export of `email-channel.ts` that `index.ts` (the package's one entry) does not re-export: no new published symbol.
4. **Grading — right, bounded, and the same on both channels.** The rewritten row error carries no `TEMPLATE_*` token and does not start with `TRANSPORT_NOT_CONFIGURED:`, so `classifyError` answers `retryable`; `classifyDeliveryAttempt` then walks `nextRetryDelayMs`'s schedule (about 1 s, 10 s, 1 m, 10 m, 1 h) and answers `dead` on the sixth attempt — there is no endless loop, worst case about 71 minutes before dead-letter. The dispatcher consults `classifyError` on the single and the digest path alike; the digest path has no template arm. `sms-channel.ts` and the webhook / http outbox never read a currency and are untouched. Every other refusal (`TEMPLATE_NOT_FOUND` / `TEMPLATE_INACTIVE` / `MISSING_VARIABLES` / `TEMPLATE_UNSUPPORTED`, and a `TEMPLATE_INVALID` after a successful read) keeps its grade — `TEMPLATE_NOT_FOUND` during a fault and "no default after a successful read" are pinned permanent on both channels.
5. **What a reader of the row now sees.** During a fault a delivery whose template needs no default is sent (pinned); one whose template has a no-argument `currency` hole is retried and the row says the organization's default currency could not be read. A `TEMPLATE_INVALID` of a cause a default cannot cure is rewritten too — ④ S1.
6. **The docs' claims still hold.** `email-templates.mdx` and `email-service.mdx` say the render refuses such a hole with `TEMPLATE_INVALID` and sends nothing, and that the refusal clears when the default is set or the hole names its code — true of the render before and after; neither page states the outbox's grade of that refusal during a settings fault, so no page moves. The drift check's `webhooks.mdx` row is the class-symbol anchor, not a claim this diff touches.

### ② Semver level

`patch` on `@objectstack/core` and `@objectstack/service-messaging` (both `private: false`, both at 18.2.0), with `Clause-②: yes (widening)` and `Metadata-protocol: none` line-initial on the PR body and in `.changeset/27257-localization-read-failed.md`, and a Before / Now / Unchanged body. **Matches the diff.** AGENTS.md Post-Task Checklist step 3 sets the level by the kind alone: `none` takes `patch`, and "a non-protocol change, widening or breaking, ships `patch`" — so core is `patch`, not `minor`: nothing a metadata author can write, no accepted value and no meaning of the hole moves; what moves is the outbox's grade of a render refusal during a settings fault, and one optional member on a runtime result type. No BREAKING banner, so no ADR-0087 disposition marker is owed (`check-adr-0087-registration` judges declared-breaking changesets only); no `Skills-docs:` line is owed (kind `none`, no `(narrowing)` arm). No `content/docs/releases/` or `CHANGELOG.md` edit. `Check Changeset` is green on this head.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Deviation (report 6508594911): the PR body's attribution lines name the card thread and its session, not the seat thread.** Accepted — the harness writes them; the claim 6507228661 declares the branch `claude/project-thread-tfwfer` as the identity record, and the branch names no issue for the same reason (the Duplicate Fix Guard warning is expected and is not a claim).
- **Landing: the PR body names the maintainer's approval of the widening as the one action needed.** Read at the reading time above, the PR carries **no review of any state** (the reviews list is empty) and no `GOVERNED_APPROVERS` approval; the PR is draft, base `main`, head unchanged. That approval is the landing precondition triage 6506866652 set, not this verdict — this record does not stand in for it.
- **`open_questions`: none.**
- **`out_of_scope_findings[0]` — #27710 (`plugin-auth` and `service-automation` fold a failed read into "no default").** Noted; this PR's shape serves it: both siblings hold the result object (`auth-plugin.ts` returns `.currency` of it, `plugin.ts` in automation does the same) and both wrappers (`withCurrency` in mail-tenant-currency.ts, `withTenantCurrency` in run-resume.ts) already catch a rejection, so #27710 is a two-site change on this member with no further core change. The memo-hit semantics (①.2) reach them unchanged.
- **Acceptance note "a persistent fault": a no-argument-currency template on an environment whose `sys_setting` read keeps failing now walks the retry ladder before it dead-letters.** Accepted as the card's own trade, with ④ S1 on what the final row says.
- **Ablations (five legs, report and PR body).** Read against the pins, each count is the one the pins predict: A1 reds the three fresh-read / memo pins of the new core file and the four fresh-read / memo-hit pins in messaging; A2 reds the memo-hit pins alone; A5 reds the two "no default stays permanent" pins plus the pre-existing permanent pin (line 35 of the messaging file). The core counts are over the NEW file alone (5 tests); the two moved pins in the existing files (`toEqual` of the whole memoized answer) would also red under A1 and A2. Not re-run here (`Local-runs: none`).
- **Premise: holds** — the removed lines of the diff show the resolver returning only `value` and memoizing the bare value, and the plugin folding both cases into `undefined`.
- **Face and tier, for the seat.** Read off the committed tree by `reviewFace`'s rule, this diff has no `packages/spec/src/**` path and no governed path, and its changeset declares `yes (widening)`, so its face is the declaration face, whose exact token under `contract-review.md` is `TIER_DEFAULT`. This record is served at `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` per the seat's brief and carries ④; no queue guard reads it (no governed path), so the landing lift is the maintainer's approval above, and nothing mechanical is owed a different token.
- **Open PRs touching these files: the dev reports none of 26.** Not re-measured here.
- **Check-runs on this head, read at the reading time above — none red.** Green (36): `Lint & Repo Gates`, `TypeScript Type Check`, `Build Core`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Test UI`, `Type Check UI`, `Build & E2E UI`, `Live E2E UI`, `Check Changeset`, `Check PR Size`, `Dogfood Regression Gate`, `Flag docs affected by code changes`, `PR-body guards`, `Plan Test Core shards`, `Test Core` shards 1, 2, 6, 7, 8, every `Lint ·` job (ESLint, PM dispatch-gates, docs & code guards, repo & tooling gates, CI / release / engine gates, the three scoped jobs), every `Type Check ·` job (workspace, source gates, consumer gates, debt ledger), `Build UI Deps`, `Auto Label`, `filter`. **Still in progress (3): `Test Core (3/8)`, `(4/8)`, `(5/8)`** — the required `Test Core` context is not answered until they complete; nothing here stands in for it. Skipped (12): the opt-in harnesses, `Build Docs`, `Lint UI`, the sharded dogfood / Test UI matrix rows, `Temporal Conformance`, `UI Published Artifacts`, the schedule gate, and the second `Auto Label` / `Check PR Size` runs.

### ④ Design judgment

For each in-scope file, against the code it cites and the scenario it is accepted against (a transient `sys_setting` fault must retry; a successful read with no default must dead-letter with the remedy):

- **`resolve-authz-context.ts` — holds.** Tried: (i) a hit returns the stored object, so the kind survives the memo; (ii) a success after a failure inside the TTL is unreachable for one key; (iii) a settings service that answers manifest defaults (`source: 'default'`, `timezone` truthy) returns early unflagged — right, the service answered and "no default" is its word; (iv) a settings refusal in front of a throwing direct read is flagged — the #10221 environment, pinned; (v) a `ql` with no `find` reads nothing and is unflagged — a composition, not a fault; (vi) the object identity shared by memo and callers predates this PR. One residual, S2 below.
- **`resolve-authz-context.test.ts`, `resolve-localization-cache.test.ts` — hold.** Two moved pins, each a whole-answer `toEqual` on the memoized failure, so each pins the memo-hit kind as well.
- **`resolve-localization-read-failed.test.ts` — holds.** Five pins: fresh flag, memo-hit flag with one read, successful-empty unflagged, #11877 unflagged, and the TTL pin on ONE engine whose backend is swapped under fake timers (the `WeakMap` key stays stable, so the pin measures the memo and not a new engine). Both doubles hold the caller's `limit` after the filter.
- **`email-channel.ts` — holds, with S1.** The read sits before the render `try`; `currency` undefined omits the key, as before; the helper's docblock states the broad match and its self-correction.
- **`inbox-channel.ts` — holds.** Mirrors the email arm through the shared helper; the new value import from `email-channel.ts` adds the edge inbox → email with no cycle (email imports nothing from inbox).
- **`messaging-service-plugin.ts` — holds.** Dropping the blanket `try/catch` is right: the resolver never throws by contract, and a `getData()` throw now surfaces as a rejection the channel grades retryable instead of being folded into a permanent "no default".
- **`template-tenant-currency.test.ts` — holds.** Twelve pins through `MessagingServicePlugin.init` + `kernel:ready` + `getChannel`, both channels, each on its own engine object. The `REFUSAL` constant paraphrases `currencyDefaultRefusal`'s sentence; fine for a token match, and the thing to replace if S1 narrows on prose.
- **`.changeset/27257-localization-read-failed.md` — right (②).**

Findings:

- **S1 — should-fix — `templateRefusalAfterCurrencyReadFault` rewrites every `TEMPLATE_INVALID` after a failed read, and drops the render's diagnosis.** `TEMPLATE_INVALID` has three causes in `plugin-email`'s renderer: a hole the grammar refuses, an `@path` value that is not a code, and the missing default. Only the third is cured by the read succeeding. A template of the first two kinds, during a persistent fault (the fresh environment the acceptance notes name), now burns the whole ladder and dead-letters after about 71 minutes with a row error that names the settings read and not the hole — the sentence the row used to carry. Bounded, documented in the helper's docblock, and self-correcting once the read succeeds, so not a FAIL. Remedy: keep the render's sentence in the rewritten error with its code spelled out of `classifyError`'s reach (strip the leading code and quote the rest as the render's refusal), or match the no-default cause alone — `currencyDefaultRefusal` is one sentence in `@objectstack/formula`, which messaging does not depend on, so a stable fragment or a sub-code from the renderer is the handle.
- **S2 — should-fix, as a follow-up card beside #27710 (outside the shape triage accepted) — the organization-less leg of the same fault is still graded permanent.** `localizationFallbackReach` turns an `AuthzStoreUnavailableError` from the `sys_organization` probe (`resolveGuestOrganization` → `tryFind`, a failed read other than a missing table) into `unowned`; no `sys_setting` read then runs, `backendFailed` stays false, and the answer is "no default" with no `readFailed`. For a delivery that names no organization under a posture with no wall, the same transient database fault the card is about still dead-letters a no-argument-currency template. The accepted shape scopes the flag to the direct `sys_setting` read, so this is not a miss against the card's grade; set `readFailed` on that leg too (without populating the memo, which #10221 reserves for the direct read), or carry it on #27710.

No must-fix. The widening is the one key triage accepted, absent on every successful answer; the memo keeps the kind without lengthening; a failed read retries along a bounded ladder on both channels; a successful read with no default dead-letters with the render's remedy; #11877 and the TTL are untouched; nothing outside the two channels changes behaviour.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `4397f06d5f45b7ffbdc6ed0ba68749b26fadfe0b`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/services/service-messaging/src/email-channel.ts, packages/services/service-messaging/src/inbox-channel.ts, packages/services/service-messaging/src/template-tenant-currency.test.ts, .changeset/27257-localization-read-failed.md (the four paths that moved between `aef05cf6` and this head; the other five files of the PR are byte-identical to the head record 6508920767 reviewed, and that record's judgments on them carry) + packages/plugins/plugin-email/src/email-service.ts (`resolveAndRenderTemplate`, `renderTemplate`, `sendTemplate` — the probe's path), packages/plugins/plugin-email/src/template-loader.ts (`load`, the read the probe repeats), packages/plugins/plugin-email/src/template-engine.ts (every consumer of the supplied `currency`), packages/formula/src/template-engine.ts (the `currency` formatter, `isCurrencyCode`, `currencyDefaultRefusal`), packages/spec/src/contracts/email-service.ts (`IEmailService.renderTemplate`, `RenderTemplateInput`), packages/services/service-messaging/src/index.ts (the package entry). Delta review on the head that answers S1 of record 6508920767; written at 2026-10-29T22:20Z, the check-run and review readings below taken at 2026-10-29T22:16Z. Commits since the reviewed head: `56a2a5cf` (code), `4397f06d` (changeset text only); merge-base with `main` unchanged.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **`templateRefusalAfterCurrencyReadFault` is now async and takes `renderWithDefault` — right, and the only behaviour change of this head.** It still returns the message untouched unless a read fault stands AND the message carries `TEMPLATE_INVALID`. Then it renders once more with the ISO "no currency" code `XXX`: a probe that renders means the missing default was the only refusal, and the row is rewritten without a `TEMPLATE_*` token (retryable, as before); a probe that answers `TEMPLATE_INVALID` returns THAT sentence, which `classifyError` grades permanent; no probe, or a probe failing any other way, keeps the retryable rewrite. This closes S1 of 6508920767 exactly as that finding asked: a refusal a default cannot cure keeps its own sentence and its permanent grade.
2. **The probe has no side effect — right.** The email channel's closure calls `email.renderTemplate` (bound), never `sendTemplate`; the inbox channel awaits the probe and discards its value (`title` / `bodyMd` are assigned only inside the first `try`). `IEmailService.renderTemplate` runs `resolveAndRenderTemplate` and returns `rendered`: the template loader's `load` (a registry read through `protocol.getMetaItemsForExecution`, no write), the required-variables check, and the three face renders. No transport, queue, persistence, outbox, hook, counter or audit row sits on that path — the only write-shaped calls in `email-service.ts` (`persistence.insert`) are in the send paths, which the probe never enters. Cost: one extra metadata read and render per attempt that already failed, bounded by the retry ladder.
3. **`XXX` is safe in every formatter path — right.** Formula's `currency` formatter accepts an argument or default by `/^[A-Z]{3}$/` (so `currencyDefaultRefusal` answers `null` for `XXX`) and formats with `new Intl.NumberFormat(locale, { style: 'currency', currency: code })`; ECMA-402's well-formedness check asks for three ASCII letters and nothing else, so no locale and no ICU build throws on `XXX` (CLDR renders it with the generic sign). The mail renderer's other consumer is the `currency:@path` branch, which judges the send's own value and never reads the default; a non-numeric amount falls to `baseString`. So a probe refusal is only ever one the default cannot cure, and the permanent grade is never reached because of `XXX` itself. The constant flows into the probe closure alone and can reach no sent mail or stored row.
4. **The no-`renderTemplate` fallback (treated as retryable) — acceptable.** `IEmailService.renderTemplate` is a required member of the spec contract, so the fallback reaches only a structural third-party sender that implements `sendTemplate` without it; there the head keeps the previous head's broad grade, and the docblock says so. The inbox channel's `renderTemplate!` is guarded by its earlier `TEMPLATE_UNSUPPORTED` refusal. A probe failing in another way (the registry read failing under the same backend fault, a template retired between the two renders) is graded retryable — right, since nothing shows the template at fault.
5. **Refusal order — right.** The real renderer refuses at the first offending hole; the `both` pin covers a template whose first refusal is the missing default and whose probe then meets the `@path` refusal: the standing refusal is returned, permanent, nothing sent. A template whose `@path` refusal comes first never reaches the probe's retryable arm.
6. **Public surface unchanged.** The helper is still a module export `index.ts` does not re-export; `EmailChannelOptions` / `InboxChannelOptions` / `EmailSenderSurface` are unchanged in type (④ S3 on the last); callers are the email and inbox channels only (grep of `packages/` and `ui/`).
